hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: If any purely expression-level rewrite makes MWCC emit `lwz r12,32(r3)` for the intermediate, the virtual-dispatch story is unnecessary. One was tried and was byte-identical (see probed_form), which supports rather than refutes it.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the four-instruction sequence, the r3-unchanged first argument and the +32/+12 offsets were all read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes.
hypothesis.statement: This is not a colouring tie-break at all. The aligned raw rows: @0xc target `lwz r12,32(r3)` against ours `lwz r6,32(r3)`; @0x14 target `lwz r12,12(r12)` against ours `lwz r12,12(r6)`; @0x1c both `mtlr r12`; @0x20 both `blrl`. That target sequence is MWCC's C++ VIRTUAL-DISPATCH shape, in which the vtable pointer is loaded straight into the call-target register r12 and refined in place. Our stream reaches the same values through a raw double-cast expression, which MWCC compiles as an ordinary pointer chase and gives an ordinary scratch (r6) to the intermediate. The source cure is to declare the object as a class with a virtual whose slot is at +12 of a vtable pointer stored at +32 (a secondary/multiple-inheritance vtable given the offset), and to call it as `obj->method(a, b)` - the retail call passes r3 unchanged as the first argument, which is exactly a `this`-call. That is a TU-shape change to movieplayer.cpp, not a one-line edit, which is why it was not executed here.

residual.signature: 13/13 insns, 2 differing words: target `lwz r12,32(r3)` + `lwz r12,12(r12)`, ours `lwz r6,32(r3)` + `lwz r12,12(r6)`
